title: Faretta Waiver (Waiver of the Right to an Attorney)
html:
SAN ANDREAS COURT, COUNTY OF:

BRANCH NAME: LOS SANTOS

COURTHOUSE NAME: {{Courthouse:select:SUPERIOR COURT|SUPERIOR COURT}}

CASE NUMBER: {{Case number=YYSCCR00XXX|##SCCR#####}}

PLAINTIFF: THE PEOPLE OF THE STATE OF SAN ANDREAS

DEFENDANT: {{Defendant name@name|FIRSTNAME LASTNAME}}

 

ADVISEMENT AND WAIVER OF RIGHT TO COUNSEL

(Faretta Waiver)

 

I, {{Defendant name@name|FIRSTNAME LASTNAME}}, personally appear before this Court and request that I be allowed to represent myself without the assistance of an attorney.

 

 

I. CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHTS

 

I certify to the Court that I can read and write and I understand that my constitutional rights include the following: 

 

1. Right to an Attorney – I understand that I have the right to be represented by an attorney at all stages of the proceedings and, if I do not have funds to employ an attorney, one will be appointed for me by the court.
 

2. Right to a Speedy Trial – I understand that I have a right to a speedy trial.
 

3. Right to Subpoena Witness and Records – I understand that I have the right to reasonable use of the process of the Court to subpoena any witnesses or any records that I may need in my defense.
 

4. Right to Confront and Cross-Examine Witnesses - I understand that I have the right to confront in open court all witness who will be called to testify against me, and I have the right to cross-examine those witnesses at the time of trial.
 

5. Right Against Self-Incrimination – I understand that I have the right to testify at my trial, but that I cannot be compelled to testify at the trial unless I so desire.

 

6. Right to be Released on Bail — I understand that I may have the right to be admitted to liberty on reasonable bail pending the trial.
 

7. Right to Self-Representation – I understand that I have a right to self-representation and may waive my right to counsel. I further understand that, if I am permitted to represent myself, I will have to conduct my own defense without the assistance of a lawyer.

 

 

II. BACKGROUND 

 

I understand that the Court must make a decision as to whether I am competent (have the ability) to make an informed, knowing, and voluntary waiver of my right to counsel. To assist the Court in make this decision, I declare and represent as follows:

 

A.  I can read and write the English language — {{-- Background}}{{A. Can read and write English:select:YES;NO|YES/NO}}
 

B. I am {{B. Age:number|##}} years old.

 

C. I am not suffering from mental illness or disability, and I have not taken any drug, medicine, or liquor within the past 24 hours — {{C. No mental illness / substances in 24h:select:YES;NO|YES/NO}}
 

D. My usual job, occupation, trade or business is {{Occupation@occupation|INSERT HERE}}
 

E. I have completed: {{Education:select:JUNIOR HIGH SCHOOL;HIGH SCHOOL;COLLEGE;OTHER|JUNIOR HIGH SCHOOL / HIGH SCHOOL / COLLEGE / OTHER (elaborate)}}
 

F. I have legal training. — {{F. Has legal training:select:YES;NO|YES/NO}}
 

G. I have represented myself in another criminal case. — {{G. Represented self before:select:YES;NO|YES/NO}}
 

H. I know the facts that must be proved before I can be found guilty. — {{H. Knows facts to be proved:select:YES;NO|YES/NO}}
 

I. I know the legal defenses that may be raised. — {{I. Knows legal defenses:select:YES;NO|YES/NO}}

 

J. I know the maximum possible punishments that are available to the Court in this matter. — {{J. Knows maximum punishments:select:YES;NO|YES/NO}}

 

 

III. DANGERS AND DISADVANTAGES TO SELF-REPRESENTATION

 

I understand that there are numerous disadvantages to representing myself, including, but not limited to the following:


A. I understand that if I am permitted to represent myself, it will be necessary for me, without the assistance of a lawyer or the Court, to follow all the technical rules of substantive law, criminal procedure, and evidence.

 

B. I understand the case against me will be handled by a prosecutor who is an experienced trial attorney, and that I will not be entitled to special consideration or assistance by the Court during the course of the trial.

 

C. I understand that if I am permitted to represent myself, it will be necessary for me, without the assistance of a lawyer, to conduct my own trial consisting of, but no limited to: making pretrial motions; making an opening statement; cross-examining the witnesses for the prosecution; subpoenaing and presenting my own witnesses; making appropriate objections and motions during the course of the trial; and making a final argument.

 

D. I understand that I cannot and will not receive any help or special treatment from the Court.

 

E. I understand that because of my custodial status, it may be difficult for me to contact witnesses and investigate my case. I understand that I may have limited access to a telephone, which will make preparations for trial more difficult.

 

F. I understand that depending on the stage of my case, if I ask to give up my pro se status and request counsel to handle my case, the Court may deny this request and I may have to proceed with trial without an attorney.

 

G. I understand that in conducting the trial, I will be limited in my movements in the courtroom. All documents, for example, will be handed to witnesses and the judge when necessary through the bailiff. I will be required to remain in my seat at counsel table and will not have free access in the courtroom.

 

H. I understand that I must not abuse the dignity of the Court. I understand the judge may terminate my right to self-representation in the event that I engage in serious misconduct or obstruct the conduct and progress of the trial. I understand that if my pro se status is terminated, I may have to be represented by a lawyer, appointed by the Judge, who will then take over the case at whatever stage the case may be in.

 

I. I understand that if at some point an appointed attorney does take over my case, that attorney may be in a disadvantaged position and that such a disadvantage will not be considered an issue on appeal.

 

J. I understand that misconduct occurring outside of court may result in restriction or termination of my pro se privileges. 

 

K. I understand that in the event of a conviction and appeal, by acting as my own lawyer, I give up and waive my constitutional right to effective assistance of counsel as a possible ground of appeal. However, if I am represented by an attorney, I may complain on appeal that the attorney did not effectively represent me.

 

 

IV. COURT'S ADVICE AND RECOMMENDATION

 

A. I understand that it is the advice and recommendation of this Court that I do not represent myself and that I accept court-appointed counsel. I understand that if I accept court-appointed counsel, an experienced trial lawyer will be assigned to try my case. I understand that the lawyer would be able to investigate my case, file pretrial motions, and advise me on what to do.

 

B. I understand all that I have read and it is my personal desire that I be granted permission by the Court to proceed pro se. I understand that by making this request, I am giving up the right to be represented by a lawyer.

 

 

V. DECLARATION

 

I declare, under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of San Andreas, that I have read this entire form. I understand all the warnings, and still wish to represent myself in this matter. I freely and voluntarily waive (give up) my right to be represented by a lawyer or have the assistance of a lawyer for my defense. I choose to represent and defend myself without a lawyer.
